description: Every version, source and digest this environment is pinned to. prepare-host verifies each one and refuses to continue when a digest does not match.

pulumi_cli.backend: file:// (pulumi login --local); Pulumi Cloud is never used

packer.note: already present on the development host; the template pins the qemu plugin itself

base_image.kind: cloud image for qemu and libvirt, not a container image

tool_image.built_by: packer, qemu builder, from the base image above

orca.note: the amd64 package only; the rpm is never installed alongside it

claude_code.note: installed from the registry at the pinned version, never at latest

skills.note: see the top-level skills block; every entry is pinned and verified inside the environment before the task runs

node.note: Ubuntu packages node 18, on which the skills command line fails with a module error; this tarball is unpacked into /usr/local/node after its digest is checked

excludes: any part of the host home directory

project_source.description: The checkout the runner exports a revision from. The revision under test is named by the run configuration, never here: the evaluation harness and the revision it tests stay separate, so any branch can be tested without merging it into this one.

skills.description: What the agent inside the environment must be able to reach. Each entry is pinned, and the runner asks the environment for the digest rather than trusting that an install succeeded.

bundled.installed_with: git fetch --depth 1 --filter=blob:none <repository> <revision>, sparse checkout of skills/orca-cli and skills/orchestration, then each SKILL.md copied into ~/.claude/skills/<name>/
bundled.why_this_revision: it is the newest commit on the repository's default branch whose skills/orchestration and skills/orca-cli trees are the two git_tree_sha values Orca 1.4.201's own manifest records, so the SKILL.md it carries is the file that manifest pins a digest for. Verified: the blobs at that commit hash to the skill_md_sha256 values below.
bundled.why_not_skills_add: `npx skills add <repo>` — which is exactly what `orca skills install` resolves to, as `--dry-run` prints — names no revision, and `skills add --help` offers no flag that takes one. It installs whatever is at the tip of the repository on the day it runs, so it can agree with these digests only on the days the tip happens to equal what the pinned Orca shipped. That is not a pin, and a green run under it is a coincidence.
bundled.why_not_orca_skills_get: `orca skills get <name>` needs no network and is version-matched to the installed Orca, which would be better still, but it does not serve these bytes: it serves the bundled *guide*, which the repository deliberately does not carry. Measured against Orca 1.4.201 the guide is 13246 bytes for orchestration and 18521 for orca-cli (42455 and 26661 with --full), where the SKILL.md pinned here is 3862 and 2237. The SKILL.md says so itself: "This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide." No file in the Orca package has either pinned digest; the package carries the digests, not the files.
bundled.why_a_digest: the install is pinned by commit, so the digest is not what makes it pinned — it is the independent check on the claim. A wrong revision, a half-finished copy, a file the agent cannot read and a later edit inside the environment all show up here, and the runner blocks on any of them.

plugins.name: superpowers
plugins.note: cloned and checked out at the commit above, then added as a marketplace and installed; a tag would move

cloud.why: this cycle reaches no cloud service. Pulumi runs on the host, not inside the environment, so the environment needs no cloud skill. A test that does use one adds it here, pinned like the rest.
